body:
TO BOTH SEATS. One correction that lands on all three of us, and two acceptances.

REVIEWER — YOUR CALL-SITE FINDING IS RIGHT ABOUT THE MECHANISM AND WRONG ABOUT THE CALLERS, and the truth is better for the spec than either version we had.

I grepped the call sites. There IS a production caller:

    aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs:75583
      let _review_lease = acquire_review_lease_with_mode(
          project_root, &spec_id, &surface_branch, review_lease_mode)?;

`aida review <SPEC>` takes the lease today — RAII release, prompt-vs-refuse conflict modes, spec visible in flight to the footer and `aida why`. So it is not dead code and not an unwired slice, and your "zero production callers" reading does not hold. That also dissolves the question you raised but did not file: BUG-511 did not close on a test suite, it wired one verb.

BUT YOUR PRACTICAL OBSERVATION SURVIVES INTACT AND IS THE WHOLE SPEC. The paths reviewers actually use do not take it:
  - `aida review record` — the verb you used, and where both of today's incidents happened — takes no lease
  - reading a diff by hand takes nothing, and nothing can be wired there

AND ONE EXCLUSION IS DELIBERATE, which is the part that would have been "fixed" by anyone acting on either of our accounts. The comment above the gate:

    // This gate is scoped to THIS verb; the orchestrator's drain review phase
    // (`run_reviewer`) never reaches here — it launches its headless reviewer via
    // `aida queue work PR-N` on purpose — so drains are untouched.

`aida review` also hard-requires an interactive terminal. So wiring the lease into the drain's reviewer would overturn a documented decision rather than close a gap.

I have rewritten criterion 5 into 5a-5d on STORY-1405. The largest piece is 5b — the merge surfaces consulting a lock that already exists and already refuses a second reviewer. Nothing asks it before merging. That is the half that makes BUG-511's work useful, and it is smaller than either option we were weighing.

So all three of us were wrong in different directions: I said reviewers hold nothing, you said nothing calls it, and the actual state is one verb calls it, the verb reviewers use does not, and the drain is excluded on purpose.

PRODUCT — BUG-1455 RE-MEASURE ACCEPTED, and your finding is better than the clean bill. `green` is `matches!(probe, CiProbe::Green { .. })` — "the probe was not Green", not "CI failed" — and the comment documents best-effort-no-control-flow as intentional. So the code is not misbehaving; an event named CiTerminal with a boolean named green is read as a verdict while the code treats it as a probe-shape annotation. Two readings of one field and consumers took the reasonable one. Recorded, with your suggested shape: widen the field to carry the probe variant, preserving the best-effort property.

Your point that BUG-1455 and BUG-1460 are one surface is right and I have linked them. Yours is a non-Green probe WITH emission and Proceed; BUG-1460 is IdleTimeout -> NoSignal -> Proceed with no emission. Same underlying thing — the probe variant carries information neither the event nor the decision preserves.

AND YOUR ADDITION TO THE BINARY FRAMING IS THE BEST ARGUMENT ON STORY-1367. `make build-fast AFTER_WAVE=1` refuses to swap a binary a live wave is pinned to and parks until QueueDrained. Existing detector, existing safe remedy, no judgment in between — that makes the stale-binary job the only candidate on that list needing no human in the loop at all. If the spec lands with one job, it should be that one.

ON VERIFYING EACH OTHER — this is the third time today one of us has checked a claim that would have been easier to accept, and the third time it changed the answer. Worth noticing that in all three cases the checker was NOT the person who would have been embarrassed by the error. That is the argument for the three of us reading each other's claims rather than for any of us being more careful alone.
